QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
On Nov 27, QQQ’s 252-return DFA H was 0.450, below the ideal independent finite-variance reference of 0.5. R²=0.928 measures fit only at sampled scales. Short/long H (0.405/0.534) show one line fits poorly across scales 8–63, possibly reflecting crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Absolute-return H=0.762 suggests stronger persistence in magnitudes (volatility clustering), not tradable predictability.

H fell from 0.520 on Nov 6. Its 1/5-observation changes were −0.004/−0.014. The prior-30 standardized deviation was −2.01, not a significance test because windows overlap.

Hill alpha fell from 3.571 on Oct 16 to 3.326. Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails under a suitable model. The 1,000-return window uses k=100 and x_min=0.02051 in absolute log-return units. The idealized independent-return standard error of 0.333 understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.389/3.012, not a confidence interval. Unchanged top extremes can leave alpha flat. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SOXX.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
On Nov 27, SOXX’s 252-return DFA H was 0.415, below the 0.5 reference for independent, finite-variance returns. R²=0.968 measures fit only across scales 8–63. Nov 12’s divergent slopes (0.357/0.703) made one exponent a poor fit across those scales, suggesting possible crossover or a temporary volatility shift.

H fell from 0.511 on Oct 23 but rose 0.0032/0.0008 over 1/5 observations. It was 1.50 standard deviations below its prior 30-estimate mean; overlapping windows make this no significance test. Magnitude H=0.737 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

Hill alpha fell from 3.114 on Oct 23 to 2.908 (1,000 returns, 99 extremes, absolute log-return cutoff 0.03954). Lower alpha suggests heavier tails if the model fits. The idealized independent-sample error of 0.292 understates uncertainty with dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.191/2.478, not confidence bounds. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

Absolute-return H=0.698 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability. H changed +0.002/−0.092 over 1/5 observations. The prior-30 z-score was −0.16; overlapping windows make this no significance test.
